name: ChartEditBench
intro: ChartEditBench 是一个面向多轮图表编辑的基准，要求模型在连续对话中维护共同上下文、根据视觉反馈修改代码并完成图表更新，用于评估 grounded chart editing 能力。
build_method: 难度控制的多轮修改链, 人工验证子集, 程序化评测
metric: Execution Rate, Instruction Following Score, Visual Similarity, Logical Code Verification
modality: 图像, 文本, 代码, 多模态
task_type: 多轮图表编辑, 代码生成
eval_feature: 执行保真度检查, 像素级视觉相似度, 逻辑代码验证
intro_en: ChartEditBench evaluates grounded multi-turn chart editing in multimodal language models. It measures whether models can keep common ground, update plotting code, and follow iterative editing instructions over time.
build_method_en: Difficulty-controlled multi-turn edit chains, human-verified subset, programmatic evaluation
metric_en: Execution Rate, Instruction Following Score, Visual Similarity, Logical Code Verification
eval_feature_en: Execution-based Fidelity Checks, Pixel-level Visual Similarity, Logical Code Verification

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2602.15758. The paper frames ChartEditBench as a grounded multi-turn chart editing benchmark for code-based chart revision. Its construction starts from structured chart specifications spanning 37 matplotlib chart types, generates executable initial charts with fixed seeds and visual parameters, and then creates progressive five-turn edit chains where early turns emphasize styling and later turns introduce structural changes such as chart-type conversion, subplots, or dual axes. Generated code is filtered through AST syntax checks, isolated execution with 60-second timeouts, render validation, and structural requirements. The verification layer uses Chart-R1 for code-to-code and chart-to-chart checks, adds instruction-following and requirement assertions, samples a human-verified subset for expert review, and evaluates models conversationally with execution rate, instruction following, code quality, visual similarity, and overall score. The review reconciles the abstract-level 5,000 instance framing with the paper statistics that report 4,142 final instances, 20,710 modification samples, and a 400-instance human-verified subset.
